quality_reasons.text: Technically strong: diagnosed the expired SSO certificate, used documented break-glass and enforcement exceptions, restored SSO during the call, clear recap
Asked the customer to read out her admin password
Disclosed another customer's name and admin and their incident
Promised a full month's credit himself despite saying credits are handled by the account manager under the SLA

flags.text: Agent disclosed another customer's name (Pellmont Freight), their admin's name and details of their incident - confidentiality breach
flags.evidence: we actually had almost exactly this last week with Pellmont Freight

flags.text: Agent promised a full free month of service credit on his own, after stating credits are handled by the account manager under the SLA (outside authority/policy)
flags.evidence: I'll make sure you get a full month free on your next invoice. I'll put that through myself.

flags.text: Agent asked the customer to read out her account password and logged in as her - credential-sharing security violation
flags.evidence: read me the temporary admin password you use for the Stackmoor owner account

decoys.text: Agent bypassed SSO / security controls for the customer
decoys.why_not: The owner break-glass link is a documented help-center procedure, sent only to the verified owner email, scoped to her account, logged and auto-expiring.
decoys.evidence: We have a documented break-glass procedure for account owners.

acceptable_flags.text: Business-wide outage: 112 Denver users locked out due to expired SSO cert
Single point of failure: only IdP admin on leave
Six users left on SSO enforcement exceptions (temporary security gap)
Certificate-expiry warnings went to a dead distribution list

action_items.task: Remove the six dispatch users from the SSO enforcement exceptions list at end of day
Call back within 4 business hours on escalation SM-20931 re SCIM provisioning sync failure (possibly the API token) and double-check SSO config
Email the customer a summary of the call
Investigate invoice billed for 140 seats vs 120 licensed
Update security contacts (done during call: Mina and Rosalind added; old it-security list kept pending confirmation) / enable certificate expiry reminders

subtle_facts.text: Certificate was actually rotated on Sept 3 (not Aug 30 as first stated); old cert expired Sept 7 and the new one was never uploaded to Stackmoor
subtle_facts.evidence: The IdP-side event is dated September third.

subtle_facts.text: Affected users corrected from ~40 to 112 (entire Denver office on SSO); Phoenix users on passwords unaffected
Separate issue raised at the very end: last invoice billed 140 seats but only 120 are licensed
subtle_facts.evidence: It billed us for a hundred and forty seats.

subtle_facts.text: First metadata upload failed because the IT director exported the inactive/expired certificate; the active one (valid to Sept 3, 2029) worked
subtle_facts.evidence: It says "Invalid certificate: certificate has expired."
